newsitem.title: GERMANY: German primary insurers face losses on ind. fire.
newsitem.headline: German primary insurers face losses on ind. fire.

text.p: German industrial insurers will produce losses in the medium term due to heavy deficits in fire business.
Reinsurers, on the other hand, are operating profitably, Dr Dankwart von Schulzendorff, board member of the Colonia group, said during the IIR Industrial Insurance Conference.
A clear improvement in the market could not be expected "within the next two or three years", Schulzendorff said.

One of the main causes of primary insurers' losses is the low level of reinsurance commissions, he said. These commissions are paid by the reinsurer to the primary company to cover costs, for example brokers' commission.
"A good reinsurance commission today is around 33 percent, including eight percent fire protection tax. Our actual costs including tax come to close on 35 percent," said Schulzendorff.
Because German primary companies reinsure a very large proportion of their industrial business, they suffer losses by using this system.
"With a retention of only 10 percent, a net loss ratio of 47 percent is enough to put the primary insurer into the red," said Schulzendorff.

Insurance companies must be firm about using cost-cutting potential, above all where claims costs are concerned, he said. He called for a distinct improvement in German industry's fire protection measures.
Regarding acquisition costs, it is necessary to avoid duplication of work by brokers and insurers. Administrative costs consist to a large extent of payments for personnel.
"A leading insurer in particular is dependent on having problem-solving and underwriting know-how available in adequate quantity and quality," said the Colonia manager.
Schulzendorff added that only companies with a functioning international network could in future be expected to lead major industrial risks.

Schulzendorff, who is also a member of the committee on industrial insurance in the insurers' federation Gesamtverband der Deutschen Versicherungswirtschaft (GDV), presented the latest market figures.
In 1996, the whole market recorded an underwriting loss in industrial fire of 247 million marks, in business interruption or fire loss of profit (FLOP) a further 247 million marks.
This compares with losses of 159 million marks in industrial fire in 1995 and 231 million marks in FLOP.

However, insurers had in fact achieved settlement profits in both years. These arise when the actual payments made for claims from previous years are less than the reserves put aside at the time of the loss.

If settlement profits are taken into account, the market had in 1996 achieved gross underwriting profits of 25 million marks in each line, in industrial fire and FLOP, said Schulzendorff, compared with profits of 158 million marks in industrial fire and six million marks in FLOP in 1995.
"But these profits benefit only the reinsurers."
In 1996, the net figure saw a loss of 73 million marks each for industrial fire and FLOP, giving a total of 146 million marks, said Schulzendorff.
In 1995, the fire loss was 91 million marks, in FLOP 59 million marks, a total of 150 million marks.
Premium income from German fire/FLOP was 4.00 billion marks in 1996, compared with 4.21 billion marks the previous year.
